title: Tailored interventions to prevent functional decline after a Sentinel Fall presenting to the Emergency Department – iSeFallED
summary: Within the study iSeFallED, older adults aged 60 years and above who experienced a fall which led to an emergency department visit receive a tailored intervention to prevent functional decline. A quick assessment battery in the emergency department will be used to determine the risk of future functional decline and to stratify participants into three arms with different interventions.  If mild functional decline is suspected individuals receive information on active aging. Persons with at least moderate risk receive an appointment at the outpatient falls clinic and can decide between either 6 months of home exercises or group training. At 4 weeks, 6 months and 12 months follow-up assessments will be conducted to evaluate functional and cognitive performance. The primary aim of iSeFallED is to evaluate the intervention and it`s acceptance, effectiveness and feasibilty. Focus groups will help to further evaluate the intervention.
conditions: fall, which led to outpatient visit in emergency department

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-  presentation to emergency department  (Klinikum Oldenburg or the Evangelisches Krankenhaus) after a fall 
- discharged within 72h
- informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- life expectancy of less than 3 months
-  unstable medical, neurological or psychiatric condition
-  bedridden or being unable to walk without support of another person
- patients, who are not able to walk without the support of another person (the use of walking aids are not an exclusion criterion, if they can be used independently
- residence more than 40 km away from the research center
- acute palliative care or terminal illness
-  social aggression or history of psychosis
-  inability to communicate verbally 
- inability to communicate in German or English, if no contact person is available in the emergency department and the home of the participant to translate
